### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. episodic ataxia, type 9  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10588)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN2A gain-of-function variant (rs...) —DISRUPTS→ SCN2A (HGNC:10588); SCN2A (HGNC:10588) —INCREASES→ Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005491); Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005491) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Neuronal sodium channel activity (GO:0005491) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251). Gain-of-function variants in SCN2A lead to hyperexcitability of neuronal sodium channels, manifesting as seizures in MONDO:0013388 and ataxia in MONDO:0030064.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration of loss-of-function variants in SCN2A in patients with MONDO:0013388 or MONDO:0030064 would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Any SCN2A variant with gnomAD allele frequency > 0.001)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting neuronal sodium channel activity could offer a therapeutic strategy for both conditions, although specificity for seizure versus ataxia phenotypes would need to be addressed.

#### 2. complex neurodevelopmental disorder  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10588)

**Proposed mechanism:** HGNC:10588 (HGNC:10588) —DISRUPTS→ plasma membrane (GO:0005886); plasma membrane (GO:0005886) —LEADS_TO→ GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0007218); GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0007218) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001257); GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0007218) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0002194); GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0007218) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of brain morphology (HP:0011331). Loss-of-function mutations in HGNC:10588 disrupt its function at the plasma membrane, leading to impaired GABAergic synaptic transmission. This dysregulation in neurotransmission underlies the shared phenotypes of global developmental delay, seizures, and brain morphology abnormalities seen in both MONDO:0013388 and MONDO:0100038.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in HGNC:10588 in a significant cohort of patients diagnosed with either MONDO:0013388 or MONDO:0100038, or the identification of distinct causal genes with non-overlapping functional pathways for each disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in HGNC:10588 in the general population that do not segregate with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving HGNC:10588 and GABAergic transmission could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring proper neuronal signaling, potentially benefiting patients with both MONDO:0013388 and MONDO:0100038.

#### 3. seizures, benign familial infantile, 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.500)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10588)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN2A gain-of-function variant (rsXXXX) —DISRUPTS→ SCN2A (HGNC:10588); SCN2A (HGNC:10588) —INCREASES→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007272); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007272) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007272) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); SCN2A loss-of-function variant (rsYYYY) —DISRUPTS→ SCN2A (HGNC:10588); SCN2A (HGNC:10588) —DECREASES→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007272). Conversely, loss-of-function variants in SCN2A impair neuronal function, also leading to seizures (MONDO:0011904). The convergence is on the shared pathway of neuronal excitability, which can be dysregulated in opposite ways by different SCN2A variants.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of both gain-of-function and loss-of-function variants in SCN2A within the same patient, leading to a mixed or intermediate phenotype, would challenge this hypothesis. Furthermore, if specific variants associated with MONDO:0013388 are found to be benign in functional studies or have a very high allele frequency in gnomAD (e.g., >1%), this would falsify the proposed mechanism for that disease. _(variant: rsXXXX)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the opposing effects of different SCN2A variants on neuronal excitability can inform targeted therapeutic strategies for epilepsy syndromes. For instance, channel blockers might be beneficial for gain-of-function mutations, while channel openers or modulators could be considered for loss-of-function mutations.
